description.narrative: Som en del av Barn- och umgdomssatsningen stödjer Sida HIV/Aids Alliansen med ett stöd i Syd Sudan med fokus på hälsa och utbildning inom SRHR.

The project includes a scaling up project based on existing presence of IHAA in South Sudan. It specifically targets young people in South Sudan and their right to access and receive youth friendly SRHR services. Focus is laid on prevention of HIV and other STDs as well as a maternal health.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2014Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: During the project period 2011-2015, the project has experienced serious challenges that have led to deviations from the original plans. However, the project has also led to a number of results, notably: -More than 1 400 000 condoms have been distributed to young persons in communities with high HIV/Aids prevalence. -More than 370 000 young persons have been given peer education on sexual and reproductive health rights, including HIV, sexually transmitted diseases, chila marriages and teen pregnancies. -50 health centers have been supported to adopt youth friendly services. -More than 450 gatekeepers, local leaders, parents and health workers have been trained on how to reduce stigma and discrimination of persons living with HIV/Aids. -The first network of young persons living with HIV/Aids in the area has been formed. -Ten health centrers have been renovated, equipped and adopted to providing youth friendly services. -More than 32 000 referrals have been made to sexual and reproductive health services. -More than 480 teachers have been trained on how to provide sex education, including sexual and reproductive health rights and HIV. -19 community based organizations have taken part in capacity development efforts to increase their capacity to effectively implement programs and report results.
In addition to this, constructive networks and collaboration have been built between rights holders, community based organizations, and duty bearers such as public health workers and key staff from local government and from relevant ministries.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
